key_insight: This paper shows that Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) can speed up RL training rollouts, but only if acceptance-rate collapse is addressed. The proposed Bebop framework uses rejection sampling to make speculative decoding remain useful during RL post-training.
problem_solved: It tackles the rollout bottleneck in reinforcement learning for large language models, where generating trajectories is slow and MTP acceptance rates often drop during training, limiting real speedups.
method: Studies why MTP acceptance degrades during RL training and identifies the main failure modes.
Introduces Bebop, a systematic post-training setup that combines MTP with rejection sampling to preserve rollout efficiency.
Uses speculative decoding more robustly so RL training can gain acceleration without relying on unstable acceptance behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means faster RL training pipelines for LLMs with less wasted compute during rollouts. It makes speculative decoding more practical for real-world post-training workflows.

paper_title: Breaking Entropy Bounds: Accelerating RL Training via MTP with Rejection Sampling
paper_authors: Yucheng Li, Huiqiang Jiang, Yang Xu, Jianxin Yang, Yi Zhang
